prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: a small painted manuscript ornament placed immediately before a section heading in a Renaissance ear-training website.
Redesign and SIMPLIFY the supplied acanthus divider terminal into ONE new compact upright acanthus sprig. Preserve the source's exact visual language: matte lapis-blue and vermilion tempera, warm worn ochre-gold, fine dark sepia outline and restrained ivory vein highlights. Preserve its softly irregular hand-painted modeling, not vector-like flatness or glossy metal.
Composition: one broad blue acanthus leaf curls naturally inward at the top, with only three clearly cut lobes; one much smaller red folded leaf opens at the lower right; a short ochre-gold curved stem unites them and ends naturally at the base. The blue leaf dominates. A little gold reverse shows at the rolled blue tip. Compact slightly asymmetric silhouette, roughly as wide as tall, with a few clean transparent notches. No secondary vine, no ivy, no miniature branches, no floating pieces. This is simpler than the reference, approximately two leaves and a stem, so it is legible when rendered only 28–32 px wide. Keep all edges and tips complete. Do not draw letters or simulate the page. No heading, text, underline, horizontal rule, badge, circle, frame, drop shadow, border or surrounding paper. Center ONE complete ornament with a narrow transparent margin on an actually transparent square canvas. Match the supplied painting's colors and linework closely.
preparation: Cropped transparent margin around alpha > 1 with 8px padding; lossless WebP, no resampling or changes to retained pixels.
delivery: AVIF quality 82; 24, 48 and 72px copies for a 1.5rem heading ornament.
